_readme: CONTRACT BASELINE. A shrink-only ratchet of client calls that are KNOWN TO BE BROKEN.

Every entry is one client call site, in desktop, iOS, Android or sip-bridge, that reaches no mounted route on the server. It was frozen on 2026-10-21, from the guard's own output, when the endpoint-contract guard (#2001) landed.

This file is not an allowlist. contract-allowlist.json holds calls that are correct, each with its reason. This file holds calls that are wrong today. Each one names the open issue that owns fixing it.
IT MAY ONLY SHRINK. When you fix a call, the guard fails until you delete its entry here and lower "size" to match. A fixed call cannot stay listed.

ADDING AN ENTRY MEANS SHIPPING A KNOWN-BROKEN CLIENT CALL. Fix the call instead. If you truly cannot, you need all of: an entry naming an open owning issue that is listed in "owners", "size" raised by one, the entry in sorted position, and a reviewer who accepts a new broken call. There is no command that writes this file.

Matching is exact: client, file, method, path (as the guard prints it) and category. There are no wildcards, and each entry absorbs exactly one call. Two identical broken calls in one file need two entries, and a third identical call fails.
Run: bun scripts/api-schema-binding/contract-guard.ts --all to see every baselined row with its line number.

owners.1701: 17 API paths the iOS client calls do not exist (contacts-v2, identity, recordings, conversation read)
owners.2002: Endpoint contract: routes the server owes (recovery-group shares/my, recovery-group candidates, contact search)
owners.2068: Webhook URLs shown to admins and registered with providers point at unmounted routes
